newsitem.title: UK: SHELL SEES GROWING CRUDE SUPPLIES HITTING PRICE.
newsitem.headline: SHELL SEES GROWING CRUDE SUPPLIES HITTING PRICE.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Thursday growing world oil supplies this year could outweigh increased demand and cause weaker crude prices.
Shell said that despite some signs of better cracker margins, it expected chemical industry margins and profitability to remain weak throughout 1997.

On crude Shell said, "Increased supplies due to the resumption of Iraqi crude exports and continued expansion of non-OPEC production may exceed demand growth in 1997. Crude oil prices could thus show some renewed weakness.
Shell reported record annual profits as earnings from oil and gas, boosted by higher oil prices and increased production, easily outweighed a substantial fall in profits from chemicals.
Current cost net profit before special items was 5.20 billion pounds, while net income on a historical cost basis rose by 30 percent to a record 5.69 billion.
Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc said that John Jennings, who has been chairman since 1993, would retire on June 30.
Jenning will continue to serve on the board, of which he has been a member since 1987. He will be succeeded as chairman by Mark Moody-Stuart on July 1.
Shell Transport and Trading, the British arm of oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group, also announced a two-for-one share split on June 26.

Shares in Shell Transport and Trading extended initial gains, rising to a record on Thursday after the oil giant posted what were generally seen as a strong set of results for the year, analysts said.
By 1020 GMT the shares were up 41p to 1,102-1/2p, but off their peak of 1,110.
